Down by Okkervil, where a rusted lamppost leans against cracked pavement,  
I peer into water tinted by last night’s rain and urban sediment.  
The bank is strewn with crumpled flyers and ivy clinging to broken brick,  
While bent, moss-clad branches murmur secrets in a language stark and slick.

Here we built our shrine from discarded scraps—a tarnished can, a burned-out light—  
A mosaic of fractured metal and ash beneath a sky bruised by fading night.  
The air still holds the tang of scorched rubber and diesel’s bitter trace,  
Each breath a measured incantation in this abandoned, secret space.

Your hand, etched with quiet scars, found mine on a weathered sleeve,  
As you whispered, “We’ve left behind the clamor for a refuge to believe.”  
Under a flickering streetlamp and a canopy of tangled, wild bracken,  
We carved a niche of solitude where no harsh reality could come to reckon.

In the hush between heartbeats, I traced the subtle lines of your intent,  
Mapping every careful contour where unspoken dreams were spent.  
While distant echoes slumbered in vacant rooms of concrete and decay,  
Our hidden spark defied the dark, a pulse that wouldn’t fade away.

The river wound its deliberate course past our forms amid scattered debris,  
Carrying fragments of forgotten days like relics of a lost memory.  
At dawn’s uncertain threshold—cold and unadorned against my back—I embarked  
On a search through murmuring currents, finding only its relentless, silent mark.
